sections.label: Our Teams

briefs.headline: Liverpool hands Barcola a possible debut at Ipswich tonight
briefs.summary: Winless after two draws and 13th on two points, Liverpool visits Portman Road at 3 p.m. ET with the £123M signing available; Ekitike, Leoni, Bradley, Gomez and Chiesa are out. The club also agreed Friday to sign 18-year-old Saint-Etienne forward Djylian N'Guessan for January 2027.

briefs.headline: Spurs leave Richarlison out of the Premier League squad
briefs.summary: Tottenham, bottom of the table with no goals and no points from two matches, omitted the striker from its 25-man list Thursday; Sky's Danny Mills said he could become "a real problem" for head coach Roberto De Zerbi. The trip to Nottingham Forest is Saturday at 10 a.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Pirates two-hit the Giants 5-2 to take the series
briefs.summary: Khristian Curtis earned his first big-league win and Mason Montgomery his eighth save Thursday at PNC Park; Oneil Cruz walked three times, once with the bases loaded in a two-run first, and San Francisco managed two hits. The Angels visit Friday at 6:45 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: WVU goes all white as Pat White's No. 5 is retired Saturday
briefs.summary: West Virginia will wear white jerseys, pants and glossy white helmets for the noon opener against Coastal Carolina on TNT, with White's number retired at about 11:45 a.m.; Rich Rodriguez said "people are still talking about what he did 20 years ago."

briefs.headline: Ohio names Nick Poulos its starting quarterback for Nebraska
briefs.summary: The graduate transfer won the job over Matt Vezza and Levi Davis on the Bobcats' first depth chart, with Duncan Brune at running back and an entirely new offensive line; John Hauser cited Poulos' "leadership, experience and physical traits." Kickoff is Saturday at noon ET on FS1.

briefs.headline: Bengals break until Monday with Chase and Higgins expected for the Bucs
briefs.summary: Zac Taylor gave the team the weekend off after Thursday's indoor practice, calling the stretch "more so like an extra game week"; Ja'Marr Chase (knee) and Tee Higgins (heel) were limited but are expected for the Sept. 13 opener against Tampa Bay.

briefs.headline: Crew add Moroccan midfielder Anass Zaroury on loan
briefs.summary: Columbus acquired the 25-year-old from Panathinaikos on loan through the 2027 season with a club option Thursday, a day after signing designated player Santiago Rodriguez; GM Issa Tall called him "a technical and audacious player." Colorado visits Saturday at 7:30 p.m. ET.

sections.label: Around the Leagues

briefs.headline: Hoshoryu shows up for the council's practice but takes no bouts
briefs.summary: The west yokozuna (grand champion) wore a brace on his surgically repaired right knee at Friday's joint practice before the Yokozuna Deliberation Council in Tokyo, did leg stomps and pushing drills against Atamifuji, and said whether he enters Aki is "uncertain until right before the tournament," Sponichi reported. The basho opens Sept. 13, nine days out.

briefs.headline: Kirishima's promotion audition draws a shrug from the sumo chief
briefs.summary: The ozeki (champion), seeking yokozuna promotion, won 10 of 16 practice bouts and "lacked forward drive," Kyodo reported, while yokozuna Onosato won 10 of 15; Nagoya champion Aonishiki skipped bouts with left-ankle pain. Association chairman Hakkaku said Kirishima's "hips are still too high," Nikkan Sports reported.

briefs.headline: Crow-Armstrong's 39th homer beats the Brewers 2-1 at Wrigley
briefs.summary: The two-run shot off Logan Henderson in the third was all Chicago needed Thursday behind seven innings from Kevin Gausman; Milwaukee (87-54) still leads the Cubs (79-62) by 8 games in the NL Central. The Dodgers scored twice in the ninth to beat St. Louis 3-2, and Toronto beat Cleveland 6-3.

briefs.headline: NFL opens Wednesday with a Super Bowl rematch in Seattle
briefs.summary: The Patriots visit the Seahawks at Lumen Field on Sept. 9 at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC and Peacock, a rematch of February's Super Bowl LX, which Seattle won; the Bengals and Browns open the following Sunday.

sections.label: In Season

coming_in.item: The youth weekend opens tomorrow, Saturday and Sunday: daily bag 6, possession and season limit 12, details on pamphlet page 40. The general season follows a week later, Sept. 12 to Feb. 28, at 6 a day and 24 in possession.
coming_in.publication: West Virginia Hunting and Trapping Regulations Summary, July 2026 - June 2027

coming_in.item: The youth bear weekend opens eight days out, Sept. 12-13; electronic registration is required and the limits are on pamphlet page 34, not in the summary table.
coming_in.publication: West Virginia Hunting and Trapping Regulations Summary, July 2026 - June 2027

prime.item: Bull-drum month on the coast; the Marine Fisheries limits page effective Sept. 2 lists an 18-to-27-inch slot, one per day, no gigging, spearing or gaffing, and every fish kept must be reported.
The same page lists a 14-to-20-inch slot with one fish over 26 inches allowed, three per day; harvest reporting has been mandatory since Dec. 1, 2025, by web form, iPhone app or paper card.

going_out.item: Day four of the two-week window under proclamation FF-27-2026, which closes at 11:59 p.m. Sept. 14: one fish per day, 15-inch minimum, harvest reporting mandatory. Carcasses can be donated for aging at a freezer at Eastern Outfitters in Hampstead.

The first gun window, in SELECTED COUNTIES only, closes Monday; the county list is on pamphlet pages 33-39 and not in the summary table, so none is named here. Registration is required, and the next window is Sept. 19-25.
going_out.publication: West Virginia Hunting and Trapping Regulations Summary, July 2026 - June 2027

sections.note: Marine Fisheries certified a 16-pound jolthead porgy caught Aug. 9 out of Wrightsville Beach as a state record Thursday, beating a 2015 mark by more than a pound. The kingfishes (sea mullet) scoping meeting in Wilmington is Sept. 17, with comments due Sept. 30. The DNR's separate migratory-bird summary is still untranscribed here, so no dove dates run.

waters.working: Down from 80.6 a day ago and the lowest of the week - the river is a chain of pools joined by ankle-deep riffles now, and every fish in it is looking up. Stay low and fish upstream: a 12-foot leader to 6X, a single ant or beetle dropped tight under the undercut banks, and a small olive sculpin swung slow through the two or three plunge pools still holding depth. Caddis, stoneflies and sculpin are the forage here, and at this flow the terrestrials on the bank are what the trout see most.
waters.note: The Forest Service is replacing the Tea Creek Campground bridge over the Williams; work began Aug. 28 with the campground and the existing bridge open through an active work zone at the entrance.

waters.near: 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.read: 25.1 ft - normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Pool water, up a tenth in a day - the wing-dam tips and the riprap are the structure and shad the forage, so a white swimbait or a spoon over the tips at first light, then a football jig dragged down the seam once the sun is on the water.

waters.near: below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.read: 25.9 ft - normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Steady below the dam after Thursday's small rise, so the current on the lock wall and in the barge cuts is ordinary again - a crawfish-colored jig pitched into the cuts and a skipjack-pattern swimbait along the riprap where the flow pins bait against it.

waters.reading: Sound highs 2:13 AM at 3.3 ft and 2:52 PM at 4.4 ft at Hampstead; lows 8:35 AM at 0.4 ft and 9:48 PM at 0.9 ft.
waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of high at 2:13 AM and 2:52 PM in the sound.
waters.working: The Fisherman's Post September report, published Tuesday and three days old, has the red drum bite "steady when fishing docks and creek mouths" on early topwater, flounder "going wild" at 20 to 24 inches with the mullet thick inshore, and Spanish and blues hit-or-miss on Gotchas off the Jolly Roger and Surf City piers; the shops are still waiting on the fall king bite. Flounder want moving water on structure, so work the flood into the 2:52 PM high; reds want the last of the fall, into tonight's 9:48 PM low. Last-quarter moon at 51%, so neap tides and a gentle inlet. Water 85.6F at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast.
waters.note: Hampstead is the sound station and the read that matters; the oceanfront pier runs well ahead and is quoted only for a surf read. NWS Wilmington's 3:46 a.m. surf zone forecast has a moderate rip current risk on Pender beaches with 1-to-3-foot surf, and a Heat Advisory covers coastal Pender and coastal Onslow from 11 a.m. to 8 p.m. with heat index values to 108.

kicker: Pat White's No. 5 is retired at Milan Puskar Stadium Saturday morning, 15 minutes before the noon kickoff.
